pl-l2d23c4-d1e108.summary: Answers whether man knew his future, his fall or the goods of obedience: things to be done were indicated to him rather than future things revealed; he had knowledge and command of what to do but not foreknowledge, so he did not foresee his fall, as said of the angels (Augustine).
claims: Adam did not foreknow his fall.

pl-l2d23c4-d1e113.summary: Concludes the treatment of man's knowledge in the first state.

pl-l2d23c4.summary: Asks whether man knew what would happen to him, his fall or the goods he would have if he obeyed. He was told what to do rather than shown the future: he received knowledge and command of what to do, but not foreknowledge of what would be. So, like the angels, he did not foreknow his fall (Augustine).
claims: Adam knew what he should do, not what would happen.
Adam did not foreknow his fall.
